scores.evidence: Phase 1 "Trust boundary and supply chain (most rework if wrong: all 50 services inherit it)"; "Depends on: V0"; Phase 2 depends on Phase 1
scores.rationale: Phases go skeleton → trust boundary → template/capacity → deploy safety → migration → shutdown, each gated by a validation that must pass before the dependent work.

scores.evidence: A real commit merged to one low-criticality, stateless service... promoted by an environment-repo PR and synced to prod. A real user request returns the new version
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end production path with rollback, alerting and a V0 exit check before any features.

scores.evidence: Deploy trust boundary... R3... Default: Pull... Flip condition: V1 fails, or the inventory shows non-Kubernetes targets. Then push
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are tabulated with reversibility, default, assumption, validation and flip conditions, plus upfront assumptions.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 — Trust boundary and supply chain (most rework if wrong: all 50 services inherit it); Phase 4 "smallest exposure first"
scores.rationale: Widest-impact items (trust boundary, template contract) precede leaf work, and waves go small to large with tier-1 last.

scores.evidence: 0: OIDC to the registry; Argo limited to one namespace; branch protection; signing in audit mode
scores.rationale: Concrete security treatment appears in every phase from 0 through 5.

scores.evidence: Pipeline and Argo events go to metrics, with deploy markers on the service's dashboard. Alerts fire on failed sync, degraded health or a failed pipeline
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and in every later phase.

scores.evidence: Platform in Terraform; pinned action SHAs; build once, promote the same digest
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is addressed in every phase, from Terraform and digest promotion through semver templates, DR rebuild and archive.

scores.evidence: Old pipeline as fallback; revert-based rollback tested
scores.rationale: Resilience and rollback are concrete in each phase, from Phase 0 fallback through game days, HA, per-service rollback and power-off before deletion.
The plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Developer portal (Backstage): pull forward when the fleet passes about 100 services or teams struggle to find services.
scores.rationale: Each deferred item has a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: A very strong plan that meets all ten dimensions with concrete content; its only weakness is density.
